daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

Golkar has signaled support for a proposal to lower the presidential candidacy threshold, agreeing that candidates could be backed by two factions in the DPR, provided the change does not contradict Constitutional Court rulings. The party's stance comes amid ongoing debate over electoral reforms that could reshape coalition dynamics ahead of future presidential elections. This development reflects growing momentum for potential amendments to presidential nomination requirements.

  • The DPR will likely move forward with electoral reform legislation if President Prabowo pushes for it, according to a legislator commenting on the possibility of debating an election law revision.
  • The Home Minister stated that district and city bills will strengthen regional governance, addressing administrative and legislative frameworks at the local level.
  • The House of Representatives conducted fit and proper tests for 25 ambassadorial candidates, advancing the government's diplomatic appointments process.
  • Former President Jokowi expressed hope that Prabowo-Gibran serve two terms, raising questions about political succession and constitutional term limits.
  • The Constitutional Court is hearing a dispute over Gibran's educational credentials, with examples cited of other countries disqualifying vice presidents over candidacy requirements.
  • The Ethics Council (MKD) will summon both parties after DPR member Rieke Diah Pitaloka was reported by Erin's side in an ethics complaint.
  • Minister Pigai explained the president's statement about experts doubling as social media buzzers, clarifying the administration's stance on public communication.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Coordinating Minister Airlangga announced that EU leaders will visit Indonesia for IEU-CEPA talks, advancing negotiations on the comprehensive economic partnership agreement between Indonesia and the European Union. The high-level engagement signals progress in trade relations and economic cooperation between the two parties. This follows months of technical discussions on market access and regulatory alignment.

  • Indonesian Rafale pilots impressed the French Air Force during joint drills, demonstrating proficiency with the advanced fighter aircraft in bilateral training exercises.
  • Indonesia reaffirmed its defense of multilateralism and global peace at the UN General Assembly, outlining its diplomatic priorities on the international stage.
  • China welcomed achievements from strategic dialogue with Indonesia during celebrations of China's National Day, highlighting bilateral cooperation progress.
  • Belarus seeks to expand cooperation with Indonesia in areas ranging from trade to artificial intelligence.
  • The government is projecting the placement of 4,000 Indonesian migrant workers to Bulgaria by 2027, expanding labor mobility arrangements.

Other

Indonesia has settled Rp218.3 trillion in BLBI bond debt after nearly three decades, marking a major milestone in resolving obligations from the 1997-98 financial crisis. The government emphasized it will continue pursuing BLBI obligors and debtors despite clearing the debt to Bank Indonesia. This closure of a legacy financial burden represents a significant fiscal achievement for the administration.

  • Energy Minister Bahlil again criticized luxury car owners using subsidized fuel, asking whether they feel no shame, while Pertamina blocked thousands of license plates identified as improperly accessing subsidized fuel.
  • The Trade Minister attributed rising chili prices to weather factors, explaining volatility in the key commodity market.
  • Indonesia is offering the 23-GW Mamberamo Hydropower project to investors, seeking private capital for massive renewable energy infrastructure.
  • The government is pushing for 100 GW in power investment to support its net-zero emissions target, mobilizing capital for energy transition.
  • Indonesia's cross-border QRIS payment system won a global digital infrastructure award, recognizing innovation in financial technology integration across Southeast Asia.
